brief: The Fed unanimously hiked 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, citing stronger growth, persistent inflation and geopolitical risk; the SEP raised growth forecasts and cut unemployment, and the dot plot shows only one more hike this year with steady rates in 2027. Raymond James reads this as a mid-cycle adjustment rather than a new tightening cycle, expecting disinflation to reassert as tariff and energy effects roll off. It ranks the hike only fourth among growth drivers behind oil, AI investment and high-income consumer spending, so impact falls mainly on rate-sensitive middle- and lower-income consumers; the 2026 GDP forecast stays at 2.3%. Historically the first hike in a cycle brings near-term equity weakness followed by gains, and the firm keeps its June 2027 S&P 500 target of 8,200 on EPS growth and lower corporate leverage. The 10-year yield topped 5% for the first time since 2007 on oil-driven inflation fears and a hawkish Fed, yet Raymond James calls current yields an attractive entry point, targeting 4.25%-4.50% by June 2027. Middle East supply disruption pushed WTI to $106; retail sales beat while housing and industrial production weakened.
